goal: Prevent large generated-project files from crossing the Provider gateway timeout by expanding high-complexity file leaves into bounded submodules, lowering the default per-file output budget, preserving interface feedforward, checkpoints, and the reviewed delivery route.
acceptance_criteria: Each generated submodule retains its own split-file checkpoint, interface feedforward, boundary receipt, and affected-only repair behavior.
High-complexity source entries with many public symbols expand deterministically into legal owned submodules plus a facade while preserving the original public path.
Provider file calls default to at most 5000 output tokens and explicitly reject length-truncated responses before publication.
The Codex conversation Provider validation, post-build finalization, local_packager, public delivery gate, and delivery manifest route remains unchanged.

quality_metrics.measure: formal provider and delivery route preservation
quality_metrics.target: kernel and provider contract tests pass without a new generation or delivery path
quality_metrics.method: existing kernel and formal provider test profiles

quality_metrics.measure: bounded context and affected-work repair at increasing project scale
quality_metrics.target: context remains within configured budgets and unrelated checkpoints remain reusable
quality_metrics.method: generation scale ladder and ACFV-scale trial

prevention: Confirm acceptance, interfaces, and applicable kernel constraints before implementation.
assurance: Review method, schema, skill, and repository instruction consistency.
Validate that support artifacts cannot authorize formal delivery PASS.
Review changed files against the kernel contract before integration.
control: Run targeted kernel and knowledge tests.
improvement: Record review findings and one bounded improvement experiment.

feedback: The former monolithic file shape now completes through bounded symbol-group leaves and a facade with no 504/520; full ACFV packaging was not rerun in this iteration.

worked: Deterministic manifest expansion, length truncation rejection, line bounds, manifest-bound checkpoints, and same-leaf retries preserved completed work and removed the observed transport failure.
did_not_work: A first 4-symbol probe still hit the token limit, and an early 2-symbol child was malformed; both were rejected before publication and drove tighter two-symbol and line-bound contracts.
experiments: Extend the same measured bounded-leaf policy to TypeScript and JavaScript only after language-specific facade/import validation and a live scale probe.
